Create one original premium photorealistic field-guide portrait of an anonymous mature Arubian Cunucu Dog, exact living local Aruban population. Text-only factual synthesis, no photograph inputs or named dog likeness.

One mature adult-looking Arubian Cunucu local dog, medium functional lean athletic build with long legs and well-developed muscular but slender trunk, neither heavy mastiff nor extremely fine exaggerated sighthound. Delicate elongated head, long real tapering muzzle with black nose and tight lips, ordinary dark almond eyes without puppy enlargement; medium triangular natural ears folded down and toward the sides, not cropped or forced erect. Developed moderately long neck and chest with normal rib volume, fairly level firm back and visible gentle tuck-up, strong loin and muscular rear. Four coherent straight foreleg and angled hindleg courses ending in four normal compact grounded paws, functional long leg proportions with ordinary anatomy. Very short smooth straight warm sandy-tan coat with fresh small white chest and toe accents, no copied named Cesar facial mask, saddle or exact markings. Natural complete attached moderately long tail rises from rump in a relaxed open upward curve with the free endpoint visible above and clear of back, no tight corkscrew, docking, stump or hidden attachment. Tail curve is one documented individual phenotype from the named adult-looking photograph, not a formal population standard; folded ears/body/muzzle/coat proportions are complemented by the local rescue guide.

Invent a fresh relaxed right-facing three-quarter standing pose, head slightly toward viewer and mouth closed. A broad dry limestone-earth trail at an Aruban low-scrub edge in warm late-afternoon light, distant quiet cactus and low rocks. Show full developed head and ears, trunk, four coherent complete limb courses and four distinct grounded paws with believable joints, weight and contact shadows. Complete natural attached open-curved tail root through free tip fully inside frame, clearly separated from back and hindlegs against uncluttered open ground. Do not recreate named Cesar, his exact tan-white saddle/black face/white mask, left profile, vegetation, collar, lead or beach composition. No windsurfing/agility or hunting action prediction.

profileEvidence.summary: Arubian Cunucus tend to be friendly, affectionate and energetic, with plenty of interest in running and play. Fetch, agility and lure coursing give that energy different outlets, while their quick leaps help them pursue lizards among Aruba’s rocks.
